chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say:

[It is] what 'Isa (Jesus) said to the disciples: 'O children of Adam, do not grieve over what has passed from you (of your world), just as the people of the world do not grieve over what has passed from them of their Hereafter when they attain their world.'
ai.seo_question: What did Jesus say to his disciples about grieving over worldly losses?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) employs a rhetorical inversion of Jesus’s (Isa) advice to the disciples, illustrating the spiritual myopia of the worldly. He posits that just as the disciples were told not to mourn lost worldly gains, those consumed by materialism feel no sorrow for their lost Hereafter, effectively trading eternal bliss for temporary pleasure. This highlights the Shia ethical emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere renunciation, but as a conscious prioritization of the eternal over the transient.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 17.Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī said, “I heard Abā al-Ḥasan (a) say, ‘

[One of the things] that ʿĪsā (a) said to the disciples was, “Do not grieve over what you have missed of this world of yours, just as the people of this world do not grieve over what they have missed from their Hereafter when they acquire their worldly objectives.”’”
